indicator_definition: This indicator measures the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) in rivers, which reflects the amount of oxygen consumed by biological processes when decomposing organic matter in water. Lower BOD values indicate better water quality. It is expressed in milligrams of oxygen per litre and is based on data from river monitoring stations.
rationale: High levels of organic pollution in rivers reduce dissolved oxygen, harm aquatic life and can render water unsafe for human use. Reducing BOD in rivers is essential for improving water quality and protecting freshwater ecosystems. Progress means a reduction in average BOD levels across monitored river stations.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected from national river monitoring networks and compiled by Eurostat in cooperation with the European Environment Agency (EEA). BOD is measured at standardised monitoring stations and represents the oxygen consumed over five days at 20°C (BOD5). Data are reported annually.
